# `•literal` — Literals

`•literal⁻ Y` writes `Y` as BPL source text, in the notation that display uses. `•literal text` reads such text back into its value without running code. The text may hold literals and the functions that `•literal⁻` writes: `ρ`, `⊂`, `,`, `:` and `•ucs`. Nested, keyed and exact values read back unchanged. Floats carry the marker of their width, `ₚ`, `ₛ` or `ₕ`, so the text reads back the same at any default width. `•hash •literal⁻ Y` hashes any array.

```bpl
•literal⁻ 2 3ρι6              ⍝ "[0 1 2◇3 4 5]ₚ"
•literal "[1 [2 3ₓ] ""ab""]"   ⍝ [1 [2 3ₓ] "ab"]
```

Errors: `DOMAIN` when the argument of `•literal⁻` holds a function or an operator, and when the text given to `•literal` holds a name, another function or more than one value; `SYNTAX` for text that doesn't parse.
